body.heading: Draw the invisible
paragraphs: Press hard with a white crayon and draw stars, a moon, and maybe a comet on white paper. Your drawing is almost invisible — white on white.
Add yellow crayon for the moon's glow. Press firmly, because the wax is going to do an important job.

body.heading: Paint the night
paragraphs: Brush dark blue watery paint over the whole page. Where there is bare paper, the paint soaks in and turns it night-blue.
Where there is crayon, the waxy drawing pushes the paint away. Your stars and moon shine through the dark like real stars in a real sky.

body.heading: Why it works
paragraphs: Crayon wax and water do not mix. The wax guards the paper underneath, so the paint cannot reach it. Artists call this trick a resist.
Let your sky dry flat. When it is dry, your invisible drawing has become a night worth framing.

takeaway: Wax crayon pushes watery paint away, so hidden drawings shine through like stars in the night sky.
safetyNotes: An adult should set up the paints and water. Use washable paints and protect the table.
screenFreeExtension: Hide a secret crayon drawing for a family member and let them paint to reveal it.
